about.title: Weed Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Weed is a small town of about 2,556 people at the base of Mount Shasta, and a sudden loss here is felt on every block. Public records for 2025 show two injury collisions in the city, two people hurt, and no traffic deaths. That is a quiet year, and we hope it stays that way. Still, fatal harm does not only come from car crashes. A fall at a job site, a delayed medical diagnosis, a defective product, or a collision on I-5, Rt 97, or S Weed Boulevard can each leave a family asking what comes next. California allows a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, and in some situations other dependents or heirs, to bring a civil wrongful death claim. That claim is separate from any criminal case and generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Weed families with an independent attorney, at no cost to you, so you can focus on grieving while someone else handles the legal questions.

whyChoose.title: Why Weed Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can explain where your family fits before any decision is made.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general two-year filing window shrinks considerably when a city, county, Caltrans, or another government entity may be responsible. Getting a claim reviewed early protects that right.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Our connection service costs nothing, and attorneys in the network work on contingency. You will not receive a bill for legal fees unless money is actually recovered for your family.

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on I-5 near Weed. Does the criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, and it proceeds independently of any criminal charges against the driver. The civil case can move forward whether or not a prosecutor files charges or wins a conviction. An attorney can also help you obtain the CHP or Siskiyou County collision reports that matter for your claim.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death, not the date of the accident. If a government entity such as a public road agency or a county hospital may be at fault, the time to present a claim is much shorter. Because the clock is already running, it is wise to talk with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: I live outside Weed but my parent died there. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Where you live does not decide your standing. California looks at your relationship to the person who died, giving priority to the spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. If you are an adult child or another relative, an attorney can review your situation and tell you honestly whether you qualify.
